s1.syndrome_frame: chronic, progressive, cutaneous vascular lesions with erythematous-violaceous patches and plaques
salient_findings: multiple, slowly growing, infiltrated erythematous-violaceous patches and plaques
firm, nonscaly, purple erythematous patches and plaques with irregular borders
thin-walled, irregularly branched blood vessels dispersed between thickened collagen bundles
key_facts: female patient in her late 20s
2-year history of skin lesions
lesions located on left upper arm and left side of chest
no triggers such as local infection, insect bite, or trauma
no fever, weight loss, or fatigue
multiple firm, nonscaly, purple erythematous patches and plaques
irregular borders on lesions
histopathological examination showed thin-walled, irregularly branched blood vessels
endothelial cells were plump but displayed no significant cytologic atypia
positive for CD31, CD34, Ki-67 (<1%)
negative for podoplanin (D2-40), human herpesvirus 8 (HHV-8)

shortlist.label: Microvenular hemangioma
shortlist.why_kept: matches clinical presentation of slowly growing, infiltrated erythematous-violaceous patches and plaques, and histopathological examination showing thin-walled, irregularly branched blood vessels

shortlist.label: Epithelioid hemangioma
shortlist.why_kept: consistent with the presence of plump endothelial cells and positive immunohistochemistry results for CD31 and CD34

shortlist.label: Tufted angioma
shortlist.why_kept: considered due to the presence of multiple firm, nonscaly, purple erythematous patches and plaques, although less likely given the absence of characteristic tufted angioma features

shortlist.label: Spindle cell hemangioma
shortlist.why_kept: possible due to the presence of irregularly branched blood vessels, but less likely given the lack of spindle cell morphology

shortlist.label: Targetoid hemosiderotic hemangioma
shortlist.why_kept: considered due to the presence of erythematous-violaceous patches and plaques, although less likely given the absence of characteristic targetoid features

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of multiple, slowly growing, infiltrated erythematous-violaceous patches and plaques with irregular borders, along with the histopathological findings of thin-walled, irregularly branched blood vessels and plump endothelial cells, is consistent with Microvenular hemangioma. The immunohistochemistry results, including positivity for CD31 and CD34, also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Epithelioid hemangioma
rejected.why: Typically presents with more distinct epithelioid endothelial cells and may have a different clinical appearance

rejected.label: Tufted angioma
rejected.why: Usually has a more distinctive 'cannonball' pattern on histology and may have different clinical features

rejected.label: Spindle cell hemangioma
rejected.why: Characterized by spindle cells and often has a different clinical presentation, including possible association with Maffucci syndrome

rejected.label: Targetoid hemosiderotic hemangioma
rejected.why: Typically presents with a distinctive targetoid appearance and may have different histological features
